title: Author of IHRA Antisemitism Definition Tells Zeteo It’s ‘So Poisoned I Wouldn’t Use It’
author: Rivkah Brown
content:
_**Editor 's Note:** We thought you might find this **Zeteo UK** piece, with
an interview with the American lawyer who was the lead drafter of the
International Holocaust Remembrance Alliance (IHRA) working definition of
antisemitism, a worthwhile read, so we are republishing it at **Zeteo**. It
focuses largely on the use of the definition in English schools, but, as we've
seen, it has had wide-reaching implications, including in the U.S., where pro-
Palestine speech continues to be attacked. _

Schools should not use the International Holocaust Remembrance Alliance (IHRA)
[working definition of
antisemitism](https://holocaustremembrance.com/resources/working-definition-
antisemitism), its lead drafter has told **Zeteo UK** , saying that doing so
could worsen antisemitism and silence discussion of Palestine.

Kenneth Stern, a prominent U.S. lawyer and Zionist who worked for decades in a
pro-Israel Jewish advocacy group, said that using the definition in schools
"creates [an] opportunity for people to hunt" teachers, making them reluctant
to teach about Israel and Palestine.

In an interview with **Zeteo UK** , Stern added that the definition - which
was never intended for use in educational settings - "requires groupthink as
opposed to giving the impetus for critical thinking" that tackling
antisemitism requires.

Sir David Bell's [review of antisemitism in English
schools](https://assets.publishing.service.gov.uk/media/6ad78a9f5eadc3d6e8a10839/Independent_review_antisemitism_in_schools_and_colleges_in_england.pdf)
was published in late October. The first of its 27 recommendations - all of
which were accepted by the government immediately upon publication - is that
English schools and colleges be encouraged to adopt the[ IHRA working
definition of
antisemitism](https://holocaustremembrance.com/resources/working-definition-
antisemitism?__cf_chl_tk=0jok33xBxLsXbSFWMbe8CJOZNnSAG3UwWPZdOoG1zh0-1793369120-1.0.1.1-wwpmMwGhkNor6LDyKII3S89nS1gtzm30wE861svSwkI)
and its attendant examples. Education Secretary Lucy Powell has since said she
_[expects](https://hansard.parliament.uk/commons/2026-10-21/debates/CAAFE9F2-EA1F-42E9-9F73-ECD65FA13C2B/AntisemitismInSchoolsAndColleges)_
schools and colleges to do so.

Bell wrote that using the IHRA definition "would improve understanding" of
antisemitism "and confidence" in how to teach children about it. Stern
disagrees.
